claims.claim: Hobb says her first choice of research source is a person who will tell her about a trade such as bee-keeping or navigating.

claims.claim: Hobb says diaries and other first-person accounts are her preferred sources for older technology.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Syl R. Martin, 2023
claims.quote: Diaries or other first person accounts are great

claims.claim: Hobb says transplanting a real person or event into an invented world is simply not believable.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Syl R. Martin, 2023

verdicts.trueWording: I like to use people as sources ... that will be my first choice
verdicts.note: Raw page read. Verbatim: 'I like to use people as sources so if I can find a person who will tell me about bee-keeping or navigating or whatever topic I'm researching, that will be my first choice.' Both limbs (people first, bee-keeping/navigating named) on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: Diaries or other first person accounts are great
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim: 'Diaries or other first person accounts are great if I'm trying to find out about an older technology.' The 'older technology' pairing is exact, but the page ranks only people ('that will be my first choice'); diaries are called 'great', never preferred over other sources.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'preferred sources' - the page says only that diaries are 'great' for older technology; the sole stated first choice is people

verdicts.note: Raw page read. Sentence appears verbatim. Both limbs covered: 'I never take an actual event ... and drop it into a book' (event) and 'I never take a person I know, change name and hair colour and insert into a book ... Each character has to be the product of the imaginary world they exist in' (person).

verdicts.trueWording: no one is bruised afterwards, there is no blood, no one limps
verdicts.note: Raw page read. Verbatim within: 'Often, no one is bruised afterwards, there is no blood, no one limps or throws up in the corner.' The screen limb is on the page: 'I'm often annoyed by movies in which the protagonist is kicked in the head...'

verdicts.trueWording: Having a good character does not protect you from physical damage
verdicts.note: Raw page read. Sentence appears verbatim in the 'Writing Traumatic Experiences' section, following 'if you get kicked in the head, you brain sloshes around in your skull'. Page sense is moral character, which the claim's wording preserves.

verdicts.trueWording: The things that happen to us change us ... what makes a character interesting
verdicts.note: Raw page read. Verbatim: 'The things that happen to us change us.' The second limb is the same paragraph: 'I think that is actually what makes a character interesting.'

verdicts.trueWording: We are all the sum of our experiences, good and bad
verdicts.note: Raw page read. Sentence appears verbatim in the 'Writing Traumatic Experiences' section.

verdicts.trueWording: Characters are shaped by their experiences. We become the product of what has been done to us
verdicts.note: Raw page read. Verbatim in the 'Hobb's Writing as a Whole' section, exactly as the claim's page field says; the page adds 'Or for us.'

verdicts.trueWording: the writer must put that character on like donning a coat
verdicts.note: Raw page read. Verbatim within: 'Creating a character who is a viewpoint character means that the writer must put that character on like donning a coat.'

verdicts.trueWording: rely on the reader to be alert and connect the dots
verdicts.note: Raw page read. Verbatim within: 'And sometimes that means that I, as a writer, have to rely on the reader to be alert and connect the dots, so to speak.' First person is the stated cause (the disadvantage of first-person narration).

verdicts.trueWording: the reader will know things that the protagonist would not otherwise verbalize
verdicts.note: Raw page read. Verbatim within: 'I like the intimacy of telling a story in the first person, because the reader will know things that the protagonist would not otherwise verbalize at all.' The intimacy limb is explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: the reader will perhaps be able to see what is coming even if the main character doesn't
verdicts.note: Raw page read. Verbatim within that sentence. 'Main character' is the first-person narrator in this passage, so the claim's 'narrator' limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: The writing and style in those books differs substantially from the Robin Hobb books
verdicts.note: Raw page read. Verbatim. 'Those books' is fixed by the question asked - whether the Megan Lindholm books will return to print in the US.

verdicts.trueWording: I think I write for people who really like to know the characters
verdicts.note: Raw page read. The quoted string appears word for word inside the page sentence, which carries a hedge ('I think I write for people...'); the claim's substance is otherwise exact.

verdicts.trueWording: you get to collect all the best bits, and then you can joggle things a bit to make them fit your world
verdicts.note: Raw page read. Verbatim within: 'The thing about researching for a fantasy is that you get to collect all the best bits, and then you can joggle things a bit to make them fit your world.' The history limb follows: 'The writer isn't locked into any exact period of history...'
